newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down, sentiment weak.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down, sentiment weak.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Thursday amid weak market sentiment, traders said.

The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 22,250 yuan ($2,683) per tonne, losing 30 yuan. It opened at 22,000 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 21,900 and a high of 22,300 yuan per tonne.
July fell 140 to 21,750, August 30 to 22,000, September rose 60 to 22,250, November dropped 40 to 22,300 and December lost 230 to 22,100 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 88,950 tonnes from 111,055 tonnes.
Copper opened sharply lower but short-covering and fresh buying pushed prices off their lows late in the session.
"Panic selling continued to emerge in the morning session but lots of buying orders poured into the market when futures prices fell below 22,000 yuan," one trader said.
"Short position holders yielded heavy profits after the sharp falls of the past few days, preferring to cover part of their positions late in trading," he said.
"Technical overselling also attracted large amounts of speculative buying at low levels," he said.
Physical prices in the Shanghai area continued to fall. With the market over-supplied, consumers were not buying, traders said, and prices were consolidating around 22,000 yuan.
In light of recent falls, and with no improvement in fundamentals in sight, market sentiment would remain weak, traders said.
"A downward channel has formed and it is now the right time to build short positions if copper prices rebound," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected to see a technical rebound in the next few days though mid-term prospects were not bright.
Aluminium ended mostly up on short-covering, traders said.
July rose 90 to 13,600, August 170 to 13,800, September 190 to 13,880, but October fell 160 to 13,860 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 2,260 tonnes from 1,600 yuan.
